purpose: Turn the twelve highest-value SAP Lead assessment routes into a repeatable study sequence built around ownership, first-wrong-decision diagnosis, evidence, and completion proof.
study_rule: Do not study the route as a product catalog. Be able to explain the business goal, decision owner, runtime path, first wrong layer, integration boundary, evidence, and trade-off in a short answer.

waves.label: Decision Chain
waves.goal: Explain how commercial and logistics decisions are created before execution starts.

waves.label: Execution & State
waves.goal: Trace execution, ownership changes, recovery, physical state, and completion proof.

waves.label: Governance & Value
waves.goal: Connect controlled master data and financial truth back to operational processes.

routes.label: Sales Order Decisions
routes.assessment_question: A sales-order value is wrong. How do you find the first wrong decision without starting from configuration?
routes.ownership_boundary: Document inputs and determination logic create values that Pricing, ATP, Shipping, Credit, Tax, Delivery, and Billing consume.

routes.label: Sales Pricing
routes.assessment_question: The condition record exists but the price is wrong. What do you prove before changing the record?
routes.ownership_boundary: Pricing procedure, condition eligibility, access, runtime key, record, and calculation are separate control layers; billing can be a separate pricing context.

routes.label: Procurement
routes.assessment_question: A PO has the wrong supplier or account assignment. Where can the first wrong decision exist?
routes.ownership_boundary: Demand, source determination, item control, account assignment, approval, receipt, invoice, and GR/IR belong to different decisions even when they appear in one document flow.

routes.label: ATP / aATP
routes.assessment_question: Stock exists but the requested quantity or date is not confirmed. How do you reconstruct the promise?
routes.ownership_boundary: ATP evaluates a requirement against supply-demand scope and business policy; Shipping and scheduling build important dates and execution context upstream or downstream of that promise.

routes.label: Shipping & Scheduling
routes.assessment_question: The delivery date is wrong. How do you prove whether the cause is plant, shipping, route, scheduling, ATP, or downstream execution?
routes.ownership_boundary: Delivering plant, shipping point, route, calendars, and scheduling build the logistics context; ATP evaluates confirmation and EWM/TM own later execution decisions.

routes.label: Production Planning & Execution
routes.assessment_question: A production order looks complete. How do you prove planning, execution, stock receipt, and financial close are all correct?
routes.ownership_boundary: Demand and MRP create the plan, production master data selects the method, execution records shop-floor reality, Inventory/EWM owns stock state, and CO settlement owns financial close.

routes.label: Integration Operations & Recovery
routes.assessment_question: The middleware message is green but the business result is wrong. What do you prove before retrying or closing the incident?
routes.ownership_boundary: Transport delivery, receiver application commit, and business reconciliation are different completion layers with different recovery risks.

routes.label: Inventory Management
routes.assessment_question: Stock is wrong. How do you explain the business event and find which state view is actually inconsistent?
routes.ownership_boundary: Inventory Management records enterprise stock events; warehouse execution, physical reality, valuation, accounting, and the source process can each own a different part of the inconsistency.

routes.label: Quality Management
routes.assessment_question: Material is blocked or unusable. How do you separate the quality decision from the logistics symptom?
routes.ownership_boundary: The inspection trigger and evidence support a quality disposition; logistics processes consume the resulting stock or process consequence but should not replace the quality decision.

routes.label: Extended Warehouse Management
routes.assessment_question: There is no warehouse task, the bin is wrong, or ERP stock does not match. How do you identify the ownership layer?
routes.ownership_boundary: Upstream processes own business demand, EWM owns detailed warehouse execution, and ERP Inventory Management remains the enterprise inventory/accounting context.

routes.label: Master Data Governance
routes.assessment_question: A change request is approved but the business process is still wrong. What does governance completion actually require?
routes.ownership_boundary: Governance decides and activates authoritative master data; replication delivers it; consuming processes prove that the governed object is usable without local repair.

routes.label: FI/CO Logistics Bridge
routes.assessment_question: A logistics document is complete but Finance still shows an open or unexpected value. How do you trace the boundary?
routes.ownership_boundary: Logistics creates the business event; valuation and account/object logic create the financial consequence; later clearing, matching, settlement, and reconciliation prove financial completion.
